title: Development of a Child-Centered Disaster Mitigation Curriculum for Early Childhood Education in High-Risk Urban Areas: A Case Study of Mataram City, Indonesia
content: Young children in disaster-prone cities depend on adults and institutions for their safety, yet Child-Centered Disaster Risk Reduction (CCDRR) is rarely embedded in early childhood education (ECE) curricula. This study developed, validated, and field-tested a disaster mitigation curriculum for ECE institutions in Mataram City, Indonesia, a city exposed to the active fault systems around Lombok and severely affected by the 2018 earthquakes. Following the ADDIE instructional design model (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, Evaluation), data were collected from March to September 2026. A needs assessment surveyed 150 ECE educators across the city. The curriculum, which combines developmental psychology with disaster management principles in three play-based modules, was validated by a five-member expert panel (Aiken’s V = 0.92–0.98). A limited field trial was then conducted in five kindergartens with 150 children aged 5–6 years and 25 educators. Paired-sample t-tests showed significant gains in children’s hazard recognition and execution of protective actions (pre-test M = 6.32, post-test M = 16.80; p < .001), and focus group discussions indicated that educators found the curriculum feasible, contextually relevant, and consistent with play-based learning. Because the field trial used a single-group pre-test–post-test design without a control group, these gains should be read as preliminary evidence of effectiveness. The study contributes a validated ECE disaster mitigation curriculum and recommendations for integrating CCDRR into early childhood education standards.
